management_steps.details: Assess for acute life-threatening target organ damage: Hypertensive encephalopathy, Stroke (CVA), ACS (STEMI/NSTE-ACS), SCAPE / Acute pulmonary oedema, Aortic dissection, Acute renal failure, Eclampsia/Pre-eclampsia.

management_steps.action: Decision Pathway: Acute TOD Present (Hypertensive Emergency)
management_steps.details: Initiate immediate IV antihypertensive therapy in ED (Labetalol or Isosorbide Dinitrate infusion). ABC resuscitation: Definitive airway if GCS depressed; NIV if acute pulmonary oedema; Fluid bolus @ 10ml/kg before IV antihypertensives. Goal: Reduce MAP by 20-25% in 1st hour (Aortic dissection: SBP <100-120 in 20 min).

management_steps.action: Decision Pathway: No Acute TOD (Uncontrolled Hypertension)
management_steps.details: Exclude reversible causes (cuff size, technique, pain, anxiety, full bladder, skipped meds). WARNING: No role in ED for stat oral antihypertensives! Treat initial presenting complaint.
True HT: Discharge on oral antihypertensive agents (HCTZ + ACE-inhibitor or Calcium Channel Blocker). Reactive HT: Reassure, no TTO. Follow up at local clinic for repeat BP check and Rx continuation.

warnings: No role in the ED for stat oral antihypertensives in asymptomatic or non-emergent hypertension.
Reduce MAP by max 20-25% in 1st hour for Hypertensive Emergencies (except Aortic Dissection: SBP goal <100-120 in 20 min).
protocol.disposition:
Hypertensive Emergency: Internal Medicine / ICU / High Care admission.
Uncontrolled HT: Discharge to local clinic for follow-up within 3-7 days with oral antihypertensives (HCTZ + ACEi/CCB).
